title: Electricity Balance Non-Validated (Discontinued, please read description)
description: This dataset is replaced by the new dataset [Generation per Production Type and Exchange](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/GenerationProdTypeExchange) and has been discontinued on January 6, 2026. It will be deleted at a later date. Updates will be published on this page and on [NEWS](https://www.energidataservice.dk/news).
comment:
Data represents the overall balance of consumption, production, import and export of electricity in an area. Production is divided into main production types.

Note that data is expressed in MWh/h, or average load, not MWh.

Data are based on upscaled real-time power measurements from the SCADA system. More precisely, the values are averages of power measurements every 4th second. **Errors will occur, and will generally not be corrected**. For statistical purposes, see [Production and Consumption - Settlement](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/ProductionConsumptionSettlement).

Gross consumption = sum of production + sum of exchange to connected areas. A positive exchange is import of electricity, while a negative is export. 

The total production is the sum of all production types.
caution:
All values in the dataset are in 15-minute resolution since 2025-04-23 12.45 CET instead of hour resolution as required by ENTSO-E. Between 2025-04-07 23.45 CET and 2025-04-23 12.45 CET and between 2025-11-21 13.30 CET and 2025-11-26 23.00 CET values are missing sporadically in connection with the transition to 15-minute resolution. The missing data will not be added to the dataset, why data in the period must be used with caution.

This dataset will not be restored to hour resolution, as the dataflow is completely integrated to the ENTSO-E data transfer.
author: Energinet

columns.description: A date and time (interval), shown in _UTC time zone_, where the values are valid. 00:00 o’clock is the first hour of a given day interval  00:00 - 00:59 and 01:00 covers the second hour (interval) of the day and so forth. Please note: The naming is based on the length of the interval of the finest grain of the resolution.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00Z. 
That is without the seconds. The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
That is without the "Z".
columns.validationRules: Always full hours, i.e. minutes and seconds are 00

columns.description: A date and time (interval), shown in _Danish time zone_, where the values are valid. 00:00 o’clock is the first hour of a given day, interval 00:00 - 00:59, and 01:00 covers the second hour period (interval) of the day and so forth.
columns.comment:
On one normal day there will be 24 intervals.

When daylight saving times shifts there will be either 23 or 25 intervals.

Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00. 
Please note that there is no time zone indicator, showing that this is local (Danish) time.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember that this is local (Danish) time.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
columns.validationRules: Always full hours, i.e. minutes and seconds are 00

columns.description: Same as bidding zone. Denmark is divided in two price areas (bidding zones) divided by the Great Belt. DK1 is west of the Great Belt and DK2 is east of the Great Belt.
columns.comment: Some datasets contain a limited number of price areas.
The expression "Load" is used as the data is based on power measurements, not energy measurement.

columns.description: Exchange of electricity towards continental Europe.
columns.comment:
A positive exchange is import of electricity, while a negative is export.

Both DK1 and DK2 are only connected to Germany until 2019, where DK1 also will be connected the the Netherlands through the COBRA connection.

columns.description: Exchange of electricity over the Great Belt connection between the price areas DK1 and DK2.
columns.comment: A positive exchange indicates a flow from DK2 to DK1, while a negative exchange indicates flow from DK1 to DK2.

columns.description: Exchange of electricity towards Norway and Sweden.
columns.comment:
A positive exchange is import of electricity, while a negative is export. 

DK1 are connected to both Norway and Sweden, DK2 only to Sweden.
A positive exchange indicates import of electricity to Denmark, while a negative exchange indicates export of electricity from Denmark.
